It's day {day}. {A} stayed up to see the sunrise from the roof, and {B} brought a blanket.
Another quiet morning on day {day}. {A} is making the rounds, and {B} is humming in the kitchen.

Day {day}. {A} gave {B} the last of the good tea and said it was the least {A_he} could do.

{A} is guarding the grain sack like it's gold. {B} says it might as well be.

{A} came back from foraging with a sack of apples. {B} is already working on a pie.
{A} and {B} traded stories over the evening meal, and there was a second helping for everyone.
{A} rations the coffee like a banker. {B} negotiates one cup a day and wins every time.
{A} dug up the first potatoes of the season. {B} danced around the garden, fork in hand.

{A} is whittling a toy for the youngest, and {B} sanded the splinters off without being asked.

{A} is learning first aid from {B}, practicing bandages on a very reluctant volunteer.

{A} is carving a new handle for {B}'s axe. The old one cracked on the last big job.
{A} is learning to fletch arrows from {B}, whose hands are slow but never wrong.
{A} is mixing a soap that doesn't smell like a dead animal. {B} volunteered to test it.
{A} built a better lamp from a jar, a wick and some stubbornness. {B} keeps it by the bed.
{A} and {B} have a running bet on whose boots fall apart first. Nobody tells them to stop.
{A} and {B} sat on the porch until late, not saying much. Good company is quiet company.
{A} lent {B} the last good blanket. It's not a gift. {A_He} wants it back in spring.
{A} beat {B} at cards again, and the stakes were dish duty for the rest of the week.
{A} and {B} made up after yesterday's shouting match, over a shared tin of peaches.
{A} is teaching {B} to whistle the old songs, and the camp will never be quiet again.
{A} keeps checking on {B}, who laughs it off but sleeps better knowing someone does.
{A} and {B} are not speaking, but both showed up to dig the new ditch. They will get there.
{A} told {B} a story from before the outbreak. It made {B} cry first, then laugh.
{A} taught the kids a card trick, and {B} is now pretending to be fooled.
{A} spent the evening on the roof, watching the sunset with nothing to do. {B} sent up a mug.
Quiet afternoon. {A} is napping in the sun, and {B} is guarding the nap from the loud ones.
{A} washed in warm water for the first time in weeks. {B} says it was worth the wood.
{A} hums while doing the dishes. {B} pretends not to listen, but the tune is catching.
{A} watched the stars with {B} after the evening shift. Plenty of room for wishes tonight.
{A} found a quiet corner and a cup of tea. {B} found the same corner and a second cup.
{A} is carving the name of every member into the doorframe, and {B} is adding the dates.
{A} read a letter from before the world ended, then folded it and gave it to {B} to keep.

{A} sat the kids down by the fire for a story, and {B} did the voices.

{A} pulled the night watch on day {day} and got a thermos of hot broth from {B} at midnight.
{A} saw a deer at the edge of the trees. {B} says leave it alone; {A} says next week.
{A} and {B} spent the foggy morning mending the nets, talking about nothing important.
The frost came early, so {A} and {B} brought the plants in and set them by the stove.

{A} and {B} are teaching {C} the watch routine. {C} has asked three good questions already.
{A}, {B} and {C} carried the heavy stove up the stairs. It is only slightly crooked.
{A} told the whole table about the fish that got away. {B} and {C} laughed anyway.
{A}, {B} and {C} shared the last bottle of cider after the watch change. It tasted too good.
{A} and {C} dug a new drain while {B} kept watch. By dusk the yard was dry.
{A} challenged {B} and {C} to a race round the yard. {C} won. {A} wants a rematch.
{A}, {B} and {C} sang by the fire until the logs burned down. The camp slept better for it.
{A} brought news from the road, and {B} and {C} drew the new route on the wall.
{A} is splitting kindling, {B} is hauling it in, and {C} is somehow supervising.
{A} and {B} patched the fence while {C} brought tea. Division of labor, day {day} style.
{A} left a few wildflowers for {D} today. {B} stood next to {A_him} for a while.
{A} wears {D}'s old scarf now. {B} says it looks right on {A_him}.
{A} and {B} told stories about {D} over supper, and for the first time they could laugh.
{A} is finishing the bench {D} started. {B} brought the nails and kept quiet.
{A} said {D}'s name at the table tonight. Nobody looked away. {B} raised a cup.
{A} still plans the watch schedule around {D}'s old hours, and {B} has stopped correcting it.
{A} planted a row of beans near where we laid {D} to rest. {B} brings water every evening.
Day {day}. {A} is steadier now than in the weeks after {D}. {B} was the first to notice.
{A} hung {D}'s old cup back on the hook. {B} said nothing and filled it with water.
{A} found a note {D} left behind. {B} read it aloud, and the camp listened in silence.

{A} chalked the new patrol schedule onto the board at the {place}. {B} corrected the spelling.

{A} restocked the first-aid kit at the {place}, and {B} signed off on the bandages.

{A} stood the night watch above the {place} with {B}. The {enemies} stayed away. Mostly.

{A} drilled {B} on the gate routine. {B} fumbled it twice and got it right the third time.

{A} strung new wire around the {place}, with {B} holding the posts straight.

{A} and {B} are reviving an old truck battery for the {place} lights. It might even hold a charge.

{A} came back from the supply run with canned peaches and a grin. {B} took half to the kitchen.

{A} taped the WLF flag back together. {B} says it looks better with the scars.

{A} wired a floodlight above the {place}, and {B} cheered when it lit the yard.

Day {day} at the {place}. {A} runs the roll call, {B} answers for the late sleepers.

{A} and {B} gathered reeds for the new roof. The hymn kept the pace.

{A} brought fresh water to the long house, and {B} sang while the pots filled.

{A} and {B} dried the fish racks in the wind, and the smell of smoke settled over the shore like a blessing.
{A} is teaching {B} to set a snare. {B} caught a finger first, and the lesson went on.
It has been a hard week, so {A} cooked the good soup and {B} found a candle to put on the table.
{A} traded a spare jacket with {B} for a pair of boots that actually fit. Both walked away smiling.
{A} walked the whole fence at dusk and found nothing wrong. {B} wrote it down, proud of the dull report.
{A} and {B} found a working flashlight in a drawer. The whole yard took turns pointing it at the sky.
{A} helped {B} move bunks closer to the stove, the first step toward a warmer winter.
On day {day}, {A} counted the people at the table and smiled. {B} noticed, and counted too.

{A} laughed so hard at {B}'s impression of the old cook that the whole table joined in.
{A} stitched the last hole in the tent canvas. {B} says it is the first dry night since the storm.

{A} walked {B} through the new watch rotation, twice, until neither could get it wrong.
{A} found the old chess set. {B} lost the first game in six moves and asked for another.

{A} and {B} kept the {place} lights on all night for the late patrol. Nobody got lost.

{A} and {B} drew a fresh patrol grid on the {place} wall. The Scars won't know what hit them.

hunger: Hungry again. I split what was left in two and ate one half. The other half is tomorrow's.
I counted the cans twice. Same number both times. It doesn't get bigger when you check.
My stomach has been growling since dawn. I keep telling it there's nothing to give.
Water, a few crumbs, and the hope that tomorrow's better. That was dinner.
Hunger makes the quiet louder. I ate slowly just to have something to do.
I went through every bag twice looking for something I missed. I hadn't missed anything.
starving: I can't remember the last real meal. I can remember the smell of it, which is worse.
My hands shake when I try to work. I sit down more often now, and stand up slower.
I boiled a leather strap today and chewed it for an hour. I'm not proud of it. I'd do it again.
Day {day}, and I'm starving. Not the figure-of-speech kind. The kind where the room tilts.
I keep thinking about food and I keep trying to stop. Neither is working.
I can feel my ribs through my jacket. Another notch in the belt. I'm running out of belt.
sick: I've got {ill_a}. I said it out loud just to hear a voice.
Mornings are the worst with {ill_a}. I lie there until I can talk my legs into it.
I know what would help: {cure}. I also know I won't find it here.
Cold sweat, bad dreams, and a long list of things I won't be able to do tomorrow.
I keep my own watch now. If I'm going down, I want to be awake for it.
I write down my symptoms so someone could read them later. I try not to think about who.
worse: It's worse today. I tried to stand and the floor had other plans.
I can feel {ill_a} settling in for good. I'm trying not to listen.
My hands won't stop shaking. I can't tell if it's the sickness or the fear.
medicine: Not a trace of {cure}. I went through every shelf in the {place}.
I'd trade everything I own for {cure}. It isn't much, but it's everything.
I keep going on cold water and bad jokes. Mostly the water.
recovery: I woke up and the worst was over. I sat in the doorway for an hour just breathing.
I'm on my feet again. Slow, with a lot of resting, but on my feet.
Beat it. Alone. Somehow that feels like it should count double.
grief: I still set out two cups in the morning. Then I remember {D} and put one back.
I talk to {D} sometimes. {D_He} never interrupts. That's the worst part.
Found {D_his} jacket on the hook today and put it on. It still smells like {D_him}.
Day {day}. I said {D}'s name out loud so it wouldn't go quiet in here.
I keep turning to say something to {D}. Habit is a cruel thing.
I wonder what {D} would have said about how I'm doing. Something kind. Something that made me laugh.
grief:illness: I can still hear {D} coughing sometimes, in the quiet. It isn't there. I listen anyway.
I keep the blanket {D} used folded by the door. Silly. It's just a blanket.
Sickness took {D} slowly. I'd give a lot for one more bad day with {D_him} instead of none.
grief:starved: {D} went without so I could eat. I know that now. I wish I'd known then.
I counted the last cans at {D}'s bedside. It wasn't enough. It was never going to be.
Every time I eat now I think of {D}. I eat anyway. {D_He} would have wanted that.
grief:attack: I keep seeing {D} at the fence, back to me, facing them. That's how I'll remember it.
{D} bought me the time to run. I ran. I haven't forgiven myself for that.
The {enemies} didn't just take {D}. They took the only person who knew my stories.
grief:lost: I keep leaving a light on for {D}. I know. I leave it on anyway.
{D} could be anywhere. Alive, even. I hold on to 'even'.
I look down the road a lot, in case it's {D}. It's never {D}. I look anyway.
grief_mercy: I did what {D} asked. It was right. It's still the heaviest thing I carry.
{D} thanked me, at the end. I'd give anything to un-hear that.
Mercy shouldn't weigh this much. {D} is at rest, and I am not.
guilt: I keep going over it. If I'd been faster, {D} would still be here. I know that isn't true. I go over it anyway.
{D}'s things are still where {D_he} left them. I can't move them and I can't stop looking.
I made a choice and {D} paid for it. That's the sentence I wake up with.
despair: Day {day}. I stopped counting the good ones. I only count how many are left to get through.
I haven't spoken out loud in days. My voice cracked when I tried. I think I frightened myself.
There's a point where tired stops being a feeling and becomes a place. I live there now.
I thought about walking out the gate and just continuing. Then I thought: who closes it behind me?
I don't cry anymore. It stopped working. I just sit, and the hours pass over me.
hope: Woke up to a clear sky and a quiet horizon. Day {day} and I'm still breathing. Today feels possible.
I fixed the roof today. It's not much, but it's mine, and it doesn't leak.
Somebody will come. Somebody always does. I'm keeping the fire lit so they can find it.
I found a seed packet in a coat pocket. Tomatoes. I planted every one of them.
I laughed today. Out loud, at nothing. Then I sat quietly and let it be okay that I did.
hope_after: {D} would have liked today. Sun, a full pot, a quiet gate. I told {D_him} about it anyway.
I ate a proper meal tonight and thought of {D} the whole time. It felt less like betrayal than I expected.
Better days, finally. {D} always said they'd come back. I'd like {D_him} to know {D_he} was right.
plenty: A full pot tonight. I ate until I couldn't move and I regret nothing.
More supplies than I can use. Strange problem to have, and I'll take it.
I made enough for two, out of habit. Ate it all anyway. Day {day}.
calm: Quiet day. I mended, I cooked, I listened. The only voice in the house was mine.
I keep catching myself waiting for an answer.
The same routine again: water, fence, food, sleep. Routine is the only company I've got.
I set my watch by the sun now. It's the only thing that still keeps appointments.
Day {day}. I'm still here. It's not a lot to write, but it's true.
I read the same three pages of an old book again. They've started to feel like friends.
The silence isn't empty. It's full of the people who used to be here.
I talked to the stove today. It listened better than most.
W
From the roof of the {place} I watched Seattle go dark, block by block. Somewhere out there the WLF is still standing, I tell myself.
W
I walked the patrol route around the {place} alone. One set of footsteps sounds a lot smaller than I remember.
W
Isaac's last order is still pinned up in the {place}: hold the line. So I hold it. One person is also a line.
W
I hold the radio to my ear every night. Static, static, and then, once in a while, a voice from far away.
W
I stand under the old stadium lights sometimes. They haven't worked in years. I stand there anyway.
W
I cleaned my rifle for the third time today. Not for any reason. It just has a right way to be done.
W
The {enemies} are out there, and I'm one person. They don't know yet. Or maybe they do. I keep the lights low.
W
Seattle used to have a skyline. I tell myself I can still see it from the {place} when the fog lifts.
S
I walked the shore at dawn and said the old words alone. The Light doesn't need an audience, they say. I'm testing that.
S
The Prophet's words are written on the wall of the long house. I read them aloud every evening, mostly for the sound.
S
I lit a candle for the Elders. I don't know if they're alive. Lighting it was my way of insisting they are.
S
The island feels bigger with one person on it. Every path I walk, I walk alone. The trees don't mind.
S
I wove for hours today, like the weavers do. Mine is crooked, but it holds. Everything crooked can hold, I'm learning.
S
The Light is a long way off today, and I'm a long way down. I keep walking toward it, one foot at a time.
S
From the harbor I watched the water for sails. Nothing but gulls. I stayed until the tide went out.
S
The Prophet taught that the Light finds anyone who keeps still long enough. I'm keeping very still.
event_warn: Tomorrow they come. I've reinforced what I can. One person doesn't make much of a wall.
The {enemies} are coming for the {place}. I sharpened everything that cuts and sat down facing the door.
The {enemies} will come soon. I said the old words, strung my bow and sat facing the shore.
event_hold: They came, and they left. I'm bleeding in two places and the gate still stands. I count that as a win.
I held. One person, one gate, one long night. I'm going to sleep for a week.
event_heavy: I held, but it cost me. Everything I couldn't carry away, I lost.
The attack is over. The {place} is a mess, and so am I. Tomorrow I'll start fixing one of those.
event_massacre: It was a slaughter. I ran, and I'm not going to apologise for it.
The {enemies} took {lost} from me in one night. I'm still counting the faces.
event_nojoin: I watched the road all day. It stayed empty.
I left food by the gate in case someone wandered in. The birds got it.
clan_won: I made it. Just me, but I made it.
Day {day}. Alone, hungry and still here. I'll take it as a win.
death_illness: {D} didn't make it through the night. I held {D_his} hand until it was just a hand. I'm the only one left.
{D} stopped coughing sometime before dawn. The quiet was worse than the coughing. Now it's only me.
death_mercy: {D} asked me to end it. I did what I was asked. I carry that by myself now.
It was the kind thing, and it was the hardest thing. {D} is out of pain, and I'm the last one standing.
death_starved: {D} starved. I had a crust in my pocket I'd forgotten about. That's what I'll remember.
There wasn't enough, and {D} told me to eat it. I did. That's the part I can't forgive.
death_lost: {D} went out and never came back. I waited at the gate until the light went. Then I waited some more.
{D} didn't come back from the {place}. I still keep the door unlocked. It's all there is left to do.
death_walkout: {D} walked out and told me not to follow. I haven't. I'm still deciding if that was loyalty or fear.
{D} left in the night. No note. I read the empty bed like it was one.
death_suicide: {D} is gone. I won't write how. I just keep wishing I had sat up one more night.
{D}: I'm angry at you, and at myself. Mostly I'm just tired, and the house is very quiet.
death_bite: {D} was bitten {ago}. I did what had to be done, and I'm not going to write down how it felt.
I keep checking my own arms for marks. {D} was bitten {ago}. I'm fine. I'm fine.
death_attack: {D} went down in the attack. I dragged {D_him} back as far as I could. It wasn't far enough.
The {enemies} took {D}. I'm still here. I keep waiting to feel like that was luck.
death_attack_many: I lost {lost} in the attack. I walked away. I still don't know why.
In one night the {enemies} took {lost}. I'm the one they missed.
loss_many: I lost {lost} in a handful of days. I stopped counting, then started again. It's only me now.
Hunger, sickness, grief, it all runs together now. {lost} gone. I'm what's left.
t_h: I'm repairing the fence. All of it.
I'm planting kale in the garden.
I'm pulling weeds in the garden.
I'm taking inventory. It's a short list.
I'm collecting wood for the fire.
I'm making a map of the area.
I'm reading an old book. Out loud, for the company.
I'm starting a fire for dinner.
I'm doing a shift in the lookout. It's every shift.
t_u: I'm trying not to think about food.
I'm too weak to work today.
I'm eyeing my boots. Not yet.
I can hear my stomach in the quiet. It has a lot to say.
I've taken in another notch on my belt.
t_s: I stayed in bed far too long this morning.
I've been coughing a lot lately.
I'm coughing up blood. I'm not going to think about that.
I'm talking to the ceiling to stay awake.
I'm showing early signs of scurvy.

hope/865ff0b0: {A} found a stack of old paperbacks in a collapsed house. Tonight there's a line to hear the first chapter read out loud.
{A} znalaz{A?ł|ła} w zawalonym domu stos starych książek. Dziś wieczorem ustawia się kolejka, żeby usłyszeć pierwszy rozdział na głos.
hope/8fd44262: {A} taught {B} how to whistle with two fingers. Now the whole camp is suffering for it.
{B} gwiżdże teraz na dwa palce, a winowajcą jest {A}. Cierpi na tym cały obóz.
hope/006fbbf9: There was a rainbow after the storm. {A} dragged everyone out to look at it. Even {B} looked up.
Po burzy pojawiła się tęcza. {A} wyciągn{A?ął|ęła} wszystkich, żeby ją zobaczyli. Nawet {B} podni{B?ósł|osła} wzrok.
hope/ad33cc76: {A} mended everybody's boots this week. Dry feet. You don't know how much you miss them until you have them back.
{A} naprawi{A?ł|ła} wszystkim buty. Suche stopy. Nie wiesz, jak bardzo ich brakuje, dopóki nie wrócą.
hope/48545543: Somebody left a flower on every bedroll this morning. Nobody's admitting to it. Everybody's smiling.
Dziś rano na każdym posłaniu leżał kwiat. Nikt się nie przyznaje. Wszyscy się uśmiechają.
hope/b8eddc1d: {A} and {B} got into an argument about the best way to season rabbit, and honestly it's the best argument we've had in months.
Kłótnia o to, jak najlepiej przyprawić królika: {A} kontra {B}. Szczerze mówiąc, najlepsza kłótnia od miesięcy.
hope/37c08027: {A} found a board game missing half its pieces. We made up new rules. {B} lost badly and has sworn revenge.
{A} znalaz{A?ł|ła} grę planszową bez połowy pionków. Wymyśliliśmy nowe zasady. {B} sromotnie przegra{B?ł|ła} i {B?przysiągł|przysięgła} zemstę.
hope/87d5e224: Two {infs} wandered past the wall last night and kept going. Quiet. {A} said it was a good sign. {A_He} said it twice.
Pod murem przeszło ubiegłej nocy {inf_two} i poszło dalej. Cisza. {A} stwierdzi{A?ł|ła}, że to dobry znak. Powiedzia{A?ł|ła} to dwa razy.
hope/ca7dbce0: {A} and {B} dragged a couch out to the yard and got a fire going. Half the camp stayed up past midnight just talking. Felt like a regular night, for once.
Kanapa wylądowała na dziedzińcu i płonie ognisko. Sprawcy: {A} i {B}. Połowa obozu siedziała po północy i po prostu gadała. Zwykły wieczór, choć raz.
hope/bcb6b6ac: Somebody found a guitar in the {place} and {A} actually knows three chords. It's terrible. Nobody wants {A_him} to stop.
Ktoś znalazł {place_at} gitarę, a {A} naprawdę zna trzy akordy. Brzmi okropnie. Nikt nie chce, żeby {A?przestał|przestała}.
hope/aa24b372: {A} got the old radio working again. Static, and one hour of music from God knows where, and we all just stood there like idiots. Beautiful.
{A} uruchomi{A?ł|ła} stare radio. Szum i godzina muzyki Bóg wie skąd, a my staliśmy jak idioci. Piękne.
hope/2eedd107: The kids were chasing each other around the {place} today, laughing, and nobody told them to keep it down. I forgot that sound.
Dzieciaki ganiały się dziś wokół {place_gen}, śmiejąc się, i nikt nie kazał im być cicho. Zapomnieliśmy, jak brzmi taki śmiech.
hope/c3b06be3: {A} has tomatoes coming in. Actual tomatoes. {A_He} won't let anyone near them, but we're all pretty damn proud.
{A} ma pomidory. Prawdziwe, już dojrzewają. {A?On|Ona} nikogo do nich nie dopuszcza, ale wszyscy jesteśmy cholernie dumni.
hope/c1666724: A dog wandered in this morning, skinny but friendly as hell. {A} named it Biscuit before anyone could vote. We're keeping it.
Dziś rano przybłąkał się pies, chudy, ale piekielnie przyjazny. {A} nazwa{A?ł|ła} go Ciastkiem, zanim ktokolwiek zdążył zagłosować. Zostaje z nami.
hope/aa8a3716: It's {B}'s birthday. Nobody remembers how old {B_he} is, so we said thirty. {A} baked something out of cornmeal and it was almost cake.
{B} ma dziś urodziny. Nikt nie pamięta, ile {B} ma lat, więc stanęło na trzydziestu. {A} upiek{A?ł|ła} coś z mąki kukurydzianej i prawie wyszło ciasto.
hope/d8489f17: Full bellies, quiet night, and not a single {inf} at the fence. I'll take it. Day {day} and we're still here.
Pełne brzuchy, cicha noc i ani jednego {inf_gen} pod płotem. Biorę to. Dzień {day}, a my wciąż tu jesteśmy.
hope/28d7bb79: {A} and {B} are teaching the kids to play cards by the stove. {B} is cheating. The kids know. Nobody cares.
{A} i {B} uczą dzieciaki grać w karty przy piecu. {B} oszukuje. Dzieciaki wiedzą. Nikogo to nie obchodzi.
hope/d76a602d: Nice enough evening that we ate outside. {A} traded a pocketknife for a jar of honey and it went around the whole table.
Wieczór był na tyle ładny, że jedliśmy na dworze. {A} wymieni{A?ł|ła} scyzoryk na słoik miodu, który obszedł cały stół.
hope/e34fcf4c: {A} strung lights from old car batteries along the {place}. Half of them flicker, but the whole place looks like something worth defending.
{A} rozwiesi{A?ł|ła} lampki na starych akumulatorach samochodowych wzdłuż {place_gen}. Połowa mruga, ale całe miejsce wygląda jak coś, czego warto bronić.
hope/c84e06df: I caught {A} humming while cleaning rifles this morning. Hadn't heard that in weeks. Maybe things are looking up.
Dziś rano {A} nuci{A?ł|ła} przy czyszczeniu karabinów. Od tygodni tego nie słyszeliśmy. Może jednak coś się poprawia.
hope/a71757e5: {B} finished the roof on the east side. First night without a bucket under the leak. Small things, Jesus, small things.
{B} skończy{B?ł|ła} dach od wschodniej strony. Pierwsza noc bez wiadra pod przeciekiem. Drobiazgi, Jezu, drobiazgi.
hope/0963e57c: We watched the sunrise from the {place} today. Nobody said much. {A} just said 'we made it another one' and that was enough.
Dziś oglądaliśmy wschód słońca {place_from}. Nikt nie mówił wiele. {A} rzuci{A?ł|ła} tylko: „Kolejny dzień za nami”, i to wystarczyło.
hope/f3c13fb3: {A} sang by the fire tonight, an old hymn from before. The whole camp went quiet, then joined in on the second verse. Her Light was with us.
{A} śpiewa{A?ł|ła} dziś przy ognisku starą pieśń z dawnych czasów. Cały obóz ucichł, a przy drugiej zwrotce dołączył. Jej Światło było z nami.
hope/caf9d3d6: The children played on the shore until the light faded and no one called them in. The Prophet would smile.
Dzieci bawiły się na brzegu, aż światło zgasło, i nikt ich nie wołał do domu. Prorokini by się uśmiechnęła.
hope/48a13cd6: {A} planted the first row of beans in the new garden. The soil here is kind. We have hope for the season.
{A} zasadzi{A?ł|ła} pierwszy rząd fasoli w nowym ogrodzie. Ziemia jest tu łaskawa. Mamy nadzieję na ten sezon.
hope/1299b27c: {B} carved a small bird for each of the little ones. {A} says the pecking order is already being negotiated.
{B} wystruga{B?ł|ła} każdemu maluchowi małego ptaszka. {A} twierdzi, że kolejność dziobania jest już negocjowana.
hope/0be30dee: We shared bread and honey at the long table tonight. {A} said the blessing and {B} laughed all the way through it.
Dziś przy długim stole dzieliliśmy się chlebem i miodem. {A} wypowiedzia{A?ł|ła} błogosławieństwo, a {B} śmia{B?ł|ła} się przez cały czas.
hope/11f0a6b8: A stray dog followed {A} back from the shore. The Elders say we cannot feed one more mouth. {A} fed it anyway.
{A} wróci{A?ł|ła} znad brzegu z bezpańskim psem u nogi. Starsi mówią, że nie wykarmimy kolejnej gęby. {A} i tak go nakarmi{A?ł|ła}.
hope/9e5c3352: {A} and {B} mended the old loom and now the weaving house is full of sound again. It feels like before.
{A} i {B} napraw{AB?ili|iły} stare krosno i tkalnia znów jest pełna dźwięków. Jak dawniej.
hope/6df7ef45: {A_title} {A} caught more fish than the nets could hold. We smoked half of it. Tonight we feast, tomorrow we rest.
{A?Brat|Siostra} {A} złowi{A?ł|ła} więcej ryb, niż pomieściły sieci. Połowę uwędziliśmy. Dziś ucztujemy, jutro odpoczywamy.
hope/b5179c54: {A} lit the evening lamps with oil pressed from sunflowers. The whole camp glowed. Her Light, even in the small things.
{A} zapali{A?ł|ła} wieczorne lampy olejem ze słonecznika. Cały obóz rozbłysnął. Jej Światło także w drobiazgach.
hope/4abee951: For the first time in weeks no one prayed for food tonight. We prayed in thanks.
Pierwszy raz od tygodni nikt dziś wieczorem nie modlił się o jedzenie. Modliliśmy się w podzięce.
hope/f5d0c17e: {A} taught the youngest the old counting songs. The whole {place} echoes with them. It is the best sound we have.
{A} nauczy{A?ł|ła} najmłodszych starych wyliczanek. Rozbrzmiewają one teraz {place_at}. To najpiękniejszy dźwięk, jaki mamy.
hope/af991a39: {B} finished the new roof on the long house. The rain came and not one drop got in. We gave thanks, and {B} took a bow.
{B} skończy{B?ł|ła} nowy dach na długim domu. Spadł deszcz i ani jedna kropla nie wpadła do środka. Podziękowaliśmy, a {B} się ukłoni{B?ł|ła}.
plenty/afe16ed5: {A} counted the stores twice. We have more than we need. Twice.
{A} dwa razy przeliczy{A?ł|ła} zapasy. Mamy więcej, niż potrzeba. Dwa razy.
plenty/dce4df09: Full pots tonight. Nobody finished their bowl and nobody wasted a bite. Hope that feels as good as it tastes.
Dziś pełne garnki. Nikt nie zostawił nic w misce i nikt nie zmarnował ani kęsa. Nadzieja smakuje tak dobrze jak to jedzenie.
plenty/a21a3c51: The supply run came back heavy. Canned beans, flour, even some sugar. {B} did a little dance and nobody will ever speak of it.
Wyprawa po zaopatrzenie wróciła z ciężkimi plecakami. Fasola z puszki, mąka, nawet trochę cukru. {B} zatańczy{B?ł|ła} i nikt nigdy o tym nie wspomni.
plenty/04ea7315: We ate until we couldn't. First time in a long time. {A} fell asleep at the table.
Jedliśmy, aż nie dało się więcej. Pierwszy raz od dawna. {A} zasn{A?ął|ęła} przy stole.
plenty/8d2989ae: There's a surplus, a real one. {B} is already working out how to stretch it into the winter.
Jest nadwyżka, prawdziwa. {B} już kombinuje, jak ją rozciągnąć na zimę.
plenty/0963b705: {A} baked actual bread. With a crust and everything. I almost cried.
{A} upiek{A?ł|ła} prawdziwy chleb. Ze skórką i w ogóle. Można się było prawie rozpłakać.
plenty/466ba3b5: The pantry shelves have gaps again, because the stacks moved to the front. Gaps between stacks, not where food used to be.
Na półkach w spiżarni znów są luki, bo zapasy przesunęły się do przodu. Luki między stosami, nie tam, gdzie kiedyś było jedzenie.
plenty/ac242da1: Seconds were offered tonight. Seconds. {A} had two.
Dokładki! Dziś były dokładki. {A} wzi{A?ął|ęła} dwie.
plenty/f2fc2441: Fucking feast tonight. {A} traded rifle cleaning kits for a whole ham. Isaac can keep his rations.
Cholerna uczta dziś wieczorem. {A} wymieni{A?ł|ła} zestawy do czyszczenia karabinów na całą szynkę. Isaac może sobie zatrzymać swoje racje.
plenty/cafb1276: Supplies are up, the {place} is quiet and everyone's belly is full. For once the only complaints are about snoring.
Zapasy rosną, {place_at} jest spokojnie, a wszyscy mają pełne brzuchy. Po raz pierwszy jedyne skargi dotyczą chrapania.
plenty/c01b8aa9: We've got more food than we need. {B} says it's a good problem to have. I say it's a miracle.
Mamy więcej jedzenia, niż trzeba. {B} mówi, że to dobry problem. Ja mówię, że cud.
plenty/2d7e16be: {A} hit the jackpot on the supply run: sealed boxes, dry goods, spices. Spices! We seasoned everything.
{A} trafi{A?ł|ła} w jackpot na wyprawie: zamknięte skrzynie, suchy prowiant, przyprawy. Przyprawy! Dosoliliśmy wszystko.
plenty/28cbb010: The kitchen at the {place} is overflowing. {B} handed out second helpings and the guard shift is in a good mood for once.
Kuchnia {place_gen} pęka w szwach. {B} rozdawa{B?ł|ła} dokładki i zmiana wartowników po raz pierwszy ma dobry humor.
plenty/91757380: Full stomachs, full magazines and a clear night. Not bad for the end of the world.
Pełne żołądki, pełne magazynki i czysta noc. Nieźle jak na koniec świata.
plenty/f6a1525c: Look at this. A whole shelf of cans, all ours. {A} keeps touching them like they might vanish. Hell, they might.
Patrzcie na to. Cała półka puszek, wszystkie nasze. {A} wciąż ich dotyka, jakby miały zniknąć. Cholera, mogą.
plenty/d93f1b1b: The granary is full. The Elders have declared a day of thanks. {A} led the blessing and {B} led the dancing.
Spichlerz jest pełny. Starsi ogłosili dzień dziękczynienia. {A} poprowadzi{A?ł|ła} błogosławieństwo, a {B} taniec.
plenty/91b69bda: The sea was generous. The nets came back heavy and the fires burned all evening. The Prophet provides.
Morze było hojne. Sieci wróciły ciężkie, a ogniska paliły się cały wieczór. Prorokini zapewnia.
plenty/3742f1fe: We have enough, and more. The little ones ate until their faces were shiny and nobody scolded them.
Mamy dość, i więcej. Maluchy jadły, aż im twarze błyszczały, i nikt ich nie zbeształ.
plenty/8228aeb7: {A} baked sweet bread with honey. The smell drifted all across the island and people came from everywhere.
{A} upiek{A?ł|ła} słodki chleb z miodem. Zapach poniósł się po całej wyspie i ludzie schodzili się ze wszystkich stron.
plenty/4f2633c3: The harvest is in. We have plenty, and the Elders ask us to remember how it felt when we did not.
Żniwa zebrane. Mamy w bród, a Starsi proszą, byśmy pamiętali, jak było, gdy nie mieliśmy.
plenty/5f129c21: Bellies full, hearts light. It is a rare thing. {A} sang until the stars came out.
Pełne brzuchy, lekkie serca. To rzadkość. {A} śpiewa{A?ł|ła}, aż wyszły gwiazdy.
plenty/223f6b36: {B} opened the last barrel of dried apples and we shared them out. Sweet and chewy and no one wanted to be first to finish.
{B} otworzy{B?ł|ła} ostatnią beczkę suszonych jabłek i rozdaliśmy je wszystkim. Słodkie, ciągnące się, nikt nie chciał skończyć pierwszy.
calm/add6f06e: Nothing happened today. Best news we've had in a while.
Dziś nic się nie wydarzyło. Najlepsza wiadomość od dawna.
calm/32e5020f: A quiet day. {A} swept the floor, {B} patched a wall. That's the entire report.
Spokojny dzień. {A} {A?zamiótł|zamiotła} podłogę, {B} załata{B?ł|ła} ścianę. To cały raport.
calm/3764da55: Rain on the roof all afternoon. {A} says it's good for the garden. {B} says it's good for sleeping.
Deszcz bębnił w dach przez całe popołudnie. {A} mówi, że to dobre dla ogrodu. {B} mówi, że dobre do spania.
calm/6e454e66: {A} and {B} traded stories about what they did before. Mostly lies, probably. Good lies.
{A} i {B} opowiada{AB?li|ły} sobie, co rob{AB?ili|iły} przedtem. Pewnie głównie kłamstwa. Dobre kłamstwa.
calm/107a0752: We counted the stores, checked the watch rota, patched what needed patching. Day {day}. Same as yesterday, and I mean that as praise.
Przeliczyliśmy zapasy, sprawdziliśmy grafik wart, załataliśmy, co trzeba. Dzień {day}. Tak samo jak wczoraj, i mówię to jako pochwałę.
calm/b227f303: {A} is trying to teach the new people to whittle. The new people are terrible. {A} is patient.
{A} próbuje nauczyć nowych struganiu. Nowi są okropni. {A} jest cierpliw{A?y|a}.
calm/a2066e50: The wind turned and the smoke went the other way. Nobody coughed for an hour. We call that a good day.
Wiatr zmienił kierunek i dym poszedł w drugą stronę. Przez godzinę nikt nie kasłał. Nazywamy to dobrym dniem.
calm/954065b0: The night watch was boring. I loved every minute of it.
Nocna warta była nudna. Kocham każdą minutę tej nudy.
calm/f225703a: Quiet at the {place} today. No Scars, no infected, no alarms. I'll take boring.
Dziś cicho {place_at}. Żadnych Blizn, żadnych zarażonych, żadnych alarmów. Biorę nudę.
calm/0350dfa9: {A} cleaned the weapons, {B} inventoried the ammo and I took a nap. Nothing to report. Day {day}.
{A} wyczyści{A?ł|ła} broń, {B} zrobi{B?ł|ła} spis amunicji, a ja ucinam sobie drzemkę. Nic do zgłoszenia. Dzień {day}.
calm/801c18f2: The radio was silent. That's either very good or very bad. I'm choosing good.
Radio milczało. To albo bardzo dobrze, albo bardzo źle. Wybieram dobrze.
calm/ad94edf4: Another day, another patrol. {A} says we've walked every inch of this district. I say we walk it again tomorrow.
Kolejny dzień, kolejny patrol. {A} mówi, że przeszliśmy każdy cal tej dzielnicy. Ja mówię, że jutro przejdziemy jeszcze raz.
calm/063cf995: The lights flickered, then held. {B} says the generator is good for another week. Another week is a lot, these days.
Światła zamigotały, ale wytrzymały. {B} mówi, że agregat da radę jeszcze tydzień. Tydzień to dużo w dzisiejszych czasach.
calm/df07ce47: Gray skies, cold wind, nothing happening. Isaac would call it discipline. I call it a Tuesday.
Szare niebo, zimny wiatr i nic się nie dzieje. Isaac nazwałby to dyscypliną. Ja nazywam to wtorkiem.
calm/1a3f55b3: Standing watch with {A}, trading jokes about the Scars' taste in clothes. Not nice, but it helps.
Stoję na warcie, a obok stoi {A}. Żartujemy o tym, jak ubierają się Blizny. Niemiłe, ale pomaga.
calm/6c1c9c2d: Another day on the island. The tide went out, the tide came in. {A} mended nets, {B} gathered kelp.
Kolejny dzień na wyspie. Odpływ, przypływ. {A} naprawia{A?ł|ła} sieci, {B} zbiera{B?ł|ła} wodorosty.
calm/1a76eca6: A still morning. The Elders led the dawn prayer and the children sat with their hands folded, almost still.
Cichy poranek. Starsi poprowadzili modlitwę o świcie, a dzieci siedziały ze złożonymi rękami, prawie nieruchomo.
calm/1425ff53: The Prophet's grace is in the small things: a dry blanket, a warm cup, {A}'s quiet humming.
Łaska Prorokini kryje się w drobiazgach: suchy koc, ciepły kubek, {A} nucąc{A?y|a} cicho pod nosem.
calm/b3557070: We carved, we wove, we ate. Nothing to report but breath, and for that we are thankful.
Rzeźbiliśmy, tkaliśmy, jedliśmy. Nie mamy nic do zgłoszenia poza oddechem, i za to jesteśmy wdzięczni.
calm/768e45db: The wind was light today. {A} says it is a sign. {B} says it is only wind.
Dziś wiał lekki wiatr. {A} mówi, że to znak. {B} mówi, że to tylko wiatr.
calm/8561fb4c: The island is quiet. The watch is awake. We sleep a little easier.
Wyspa jest cicha. Straż czuwa. Śpimy trochę spokojniej.
calm/4377405f: {A} and {B} sat at the dock and watched the fog roll in. There was nothing to say, and nothing needed to be.
{A} i {B} siedzi{AB?eli|ały} na pomoście i patrz{AB?yli|yły}, jak nadciąga mgła. Nie było o czym mówić i nie trzeba było.
join/8387e653: {A} wandered in this morning, half-starved and covered in dust. {B} gave {A_him} a bowl of soup and a blanket.
{A} {A?przywlókł|przywlekła} się dziś rano, na wpół zagłodzon{A?y|a} i cał{A?y|a} w kurzu. {B} dał{B?|a} {A?mu|jej} miskę zupy i koc.
join/d8a7bc97: Someone new showed up at the gate. {A}. Says {A_he} heard we had food. We do, barely. {A_He}'s staying.
Ktoś nowy zjawił się przy bramie. {A}. Mówi, że słyszał{A?|a}, że mamy jedzenie. Mamy, ledwo. Zostaje z nami.

exp_leave~ff33a6ca.pl: {A}, {B} i {C} wychodzą gęsiego, łuki nienapięte, dopóki brzeg nie zostanie za nimi. Najpierw {dest}, potem {goal}, potem dom.

exp_leave~20f59dc6.en: {A} and {B} wrap their boots in plastic bags against the wet and leave for {dest}. The trip is for {goal}.
exp_leave~20f59dc6.pl: {A} i {B} owijają buty foliowymi torbami przed wilgocią i ruszają {dest_to}. Chodzi o {goal_acc}.

exp_leave~713b4aa3.en: {A} chalks the date on the gate post before leaving for {dest} with {B}. Whoever wipes it off has to explain why.
exp_leave~713b4aa3.pl: {A} kreśli kredą datę na słupku bramy. Potem {A} i {B} ruszają {dest_to}. Kto zetrze datę, będzie musiał się tłumaczyć.

exp_leave~be633482.en: {B} counts the shells in {B_his} pocket twice and {A} pretends not to notice. They leave for {dest} at first light, after {goal}.
exp_leave~be633482.pl: {B} dwa razy liczy naboje w kieszeni, a {A} udaje, że tego nie widzi. O pierwszym brzasku ruszają {dest_to} po {goal_acc}.

exp_leave~93fac4e2.en: {A} takes the good flashlight, the one with the taped switch, and {B} takes the bad one. {dest}, for {goal}, back {nd_in}.
exp_leave~93fac4e2.pl: {A} bierze dobrą latarkę, tę z oklejonym włącznikiem, a {B} tę gorszą. Cel: {dest}, po {goal_acc}, powrót {nd_in}.

exp_leave~f9a835d4.en: There is a list of who went to {dest} last and who came back. {A} and {B} read it before they go, and go anyway. They want {goal}.
exp_leave~f9a835d4.pl: Jest lista tych, którzy ostatnio szli {dest_to}, i tych, którzy wrócili. {A} i {B} czytają ją przed wyjściem i mimo to idą. Chcą {goal_gen}.

exp_leave~9a04b008.en: {A} kisses the doorframe on the way out, a habit {A_he} will not explain. {B} follows {A_him} towards {dest} looking for {goal}.
exp_leave~9a04b008.pl: {A} całuje framugę na wyjściu, z przyzwyczajenia, którego nie chce wyjaśnić. {B} rusza za {A?nim|nią} {dest_to}, po {goal_acc}.

exp_leave~80a85319.en: {A} and {B} set out for {dest} in a good mood, racing each other to the end of the road and then walking like adults. They are after {goal}.
exp_leave~80a85319.pl: {A} i {B} wyruszają {dest_to} w dobrym humorze: ścigają się do końca drogi, a potem idą już jak dorośli. Chodzi o {goal_acc}.

exp_leave~1c7f805a.en: {A} is not well rested and {B} is not well fed, and {dest} does not care. They leave for {goal} before anyone can talk them out of it.
exp_leave~1c7f805a.pl: {A} jest zmęczon{A?y|a}, {B} jest głodn{B?y|a}, a {dest} nie ma to żadnego znaczenia. Wyruszają po {goal_acc}, zanim ktokolwiek ich od tego odwiedzie.

exp_leave~2fb326b0.en: {A} oils the hinges of the gate so nobody hears them leave. {B} carries two empty sacks for {goal}. {dest} is {nd_in} away and back.
exp_leave~2fb326b0.pl: {A} oliwi zawiasy bramy, żeby nikt nie usłyszał wyjścia. {B} niesie dwa puste worki na {goal_acc}. {dest}: tam i z powrotem {nd_in}.

exp_leave~9e2bee28.en: The last party to see {dest} drew a skull on the map next to it. {A} draws a smaller skull next to that one, and leaves with {B} for {goal}.
exp_leave~9e2bee28.pl: Ostatnia grupa, która była {dest_at}, narysowała obok na mapie czaszkę. {A} rysuje obok drugą, mniejszą. Potem {A} i {B} ruszają po {goal_acc}.

exp_leave~aa9bb47b.en: {A}, {B} and {C} leave for {dest} with a single compass between them and three opinions about it. The job is {goal}.
exp_leave~aa9bb47b.pl: {A}, {B} i {C} ruszają {dest_to} z jednym kompasem na troje i z trzema zdaniami na jego temat. Zadanie: {goal}.

exp_leave~65bba0cb.en: {B} asks {A} what they do if {dest} is already picked clean. {A} says then they bring back the story. They go for {goal}.
exp_leave~65bba0cb.pl: {B} pyta, co zrobią, jeśli {dest_at} nic już nie zostało. {A} odpowiada, że wtedy przyniosą chociaż historię. Idą po {goal_acc}.

exp_leave~29864067.en: {A} signs the patrol book at the gate: two names, {dest}, {goal}, back {nd_in}. The guard adds a question mark after the last part.
exp_leave~29864067.pl: {A} wpisuje się do książki patroli przy bramie: dwa nazwiska, {dest}, {goal}, powrót {nd_in}. Wartownik dopisuje znak zapytania po ostatnim punkcie.

exp_leave~52d6af17.en: {A} and {B} get a ration of rounds from the quartermaster, counted out one at a time on a cloth, and leave for {dest} to look for {goal}.
exp_leave~52d6af17.pl: {A} i {B} dostają od kwatermistrza przydział naboi, wyliczany po jednym na szmatce, i ruszają {dest_to} szukać {goal_gen}.

exp_leave~27f6b6a9.en: Two dogs go with {A} and {B} to {dest}, and only one of them is any use. Isaac signed for {goal}; the dogs signed for nothing.
exp_leave~27f6b6a9.pl: {A} i {B} idą {dest_to} z dwoma psami, a pożytek jest tylko z jednego. Isaac podpisał rozkaz w sprawie {goal_gen}; psy niczego nie podpisywały.

exp_leave~aad30c72.en: {A}, {B} and {C} leave the stadium by the service tunnel, the one with the dead bulb, for {dest}. They want {goal}.
exp_leave~aad30c72.pl: {A}, {B} i {C} opuszczają stadion tunelem technicznym, tym z przepaloną żarówką, i idą {dest_to}. Chcą {goal_gen}.

exp_leave~6d0b4811.en: {A} braids a strand of red thread into {B}'s hair for the road, and they leave for {dest} by the shore path. The island needs {goal}.
exp_leave~6d0b4811.pl: {A} wplata na drogę czerwoną nić we włosy, które nadstawia {B}. Potem ścieżką brzegiem ruszają {dest_to}. Wyspa potrzebuje {goal_gen}.

exp_leave~da590fe9.en: {A} and {B} take the low path to {dest}, whistling the three notes that mean 'friend' to the lookouts in the trees. They are after {goal}.
exp_leave~da590fe9.pl: {A} i {B} idą dolną ścieżką {dest_to}, gwiżdżąc do czujek na drzewach trzy nuty, które znaczą 'swój'. Chodzi o {goal_acc}.

exp_leave~9c2bbcb6.en: The elders bless the boat and {A} and {B} row for {dest} with the tide. Neither of them likes the water. Both of them want {goal}.
exp_leave~9c2bbcb6.pl: Starsi błogosławią łódź, a {A} i {B} wiosłują z pływem {dest_to}. Żadne z nich nie lubi wody. Oboje chcą {goal_gen}.

exp_leave~e5115e0e.en: {A}, {B} and {C} walk out of the gate in silence, as the Prophet taught: words are for the return. {dest}, for {goal}.
exp_leave~e5115e0e.pl: {A}, {B} i {C} wychodzą przez bramę w milczeniu, jak uczył Prorok: słowa są na powrót. Cel: {dest}, po {goal_acc}.

exp_wait~320fa5f4.en: {B} left for {dest} {nd_ago}. {A} has stopped pretending not to watch the gate.
exp_wait~320fa5f4.pl: {B} wyruszył{B?|a} {dest_to} {nd_ago}. {A} przestał{A?|a} udawać, że nie patrzy na bramę.

exp_wait~7fd40f92.en: {A} leaves a lamp lit in the window for {B}. {B} is still out at {dest}.
exp_wait~7fd40f92.pl: {A} zostawia w oknie zapaloną lampę dla {B?niego|niej}. {B} wciąż jest {dest_at}.

exp_wait~ebcc00b3.en: There has been no word from {B} since {B_he} left. {A} says it is the radio. Nobody believes it is the radio.
exp_wait~ebcc00b3.pl: {B} {B?wyszedł|wyszła}, a od tamtej pory nie ma żadnych wieści. {A} mówi, że to radio. Nikt nie wierzy, że to radio.

exp_wait~e5670c4a.en: There has been no word from {B} since {B_he} left. {A} says the tide is late. Nobody believes it is the tide.
exp_wait~e5670c4a.pl: {B} {B?wyszedł|wyszła}, a od tamtej pory nie ma żadnych wieści. {A} mówi, że to przez pływ. Nikt nie wierzy, że to przez pływ.

exp_wait~e71120f5.en: {A} asks the gate watch twice an hour whether {B} is back from {dest} yet.
exp_wait~e71120f5.pl: {A} co godzinę pyta wartę przy bramie, czy {B} już wrócił{B?|a} {dest_from}.

exp_wait~b6affd46.en: Supper is kept warm for {B}, who should be back from {dest} by now. {A} tells everyone not to worry, in a voice that is not worried.
exp_wait~b6affd46.pl: Ktoś trzyma ciepłą kolację: {B} powin{B?ien|na} być już z powrotem {dest_from}. {A} mówi wszystkim, żeby się nie martwili, głosem, który się nie martwi.

exp_wait~2cfd55d7.en: {A} cleans {B}'s spare boots, though they are clean. {B} left for {dest} {nd_ago}.
exp_wait~2cfd55d7.pl: {A} czyści zapasowe buty, które zostawił{B?|a} {B}, choć są czyste. {B} {B?wyszedł|wyszła} {dest_to} {nd_ago}.

exp_wait~c697ab28.en: {A} has a theory about how long {dest} should take and keeps adjusting it. {B} left {nd_ago}.
exp_wait~c697ab28.pl: {A} ma teorię, ile powinna trwać wyprawa {dest_to}, i ciągle ją poprawia. {B} {B?wyszedł|wyszła} {nd_ago}.

exp_wait~e4d2c0ba.en: Nobody sits in {B}'s place at supper. {A} sets out a bowl anyway, and it goes cold. {B} is still at {dest}.
exp_wait~e4d2c0ba.pl: Przy kolacji nikt nie siada na miejscu, które zajmuje {B}. {A} i tak stawia tam miskę, która stygnie. {B} wciąż jest {dest_at}.

exp_ret_good~8fd67005.en: {A} and {B} are back from {dest} {nd_after}, loaded down with {goal}. Nobody asks how it went; the bags say enough.
exp_ret_good~8fd67005.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {dest_from} {nd_after}, obładowani {goal_ins}. Nikt nie pyta, jak poszło; torby mówią same za siebie.

exp_ret_good~a9cbe0ea.en: The party comes home from {dest} {nd_after} with {goal}. {A} sets the haul on the table and counts it twice.
exp_ret_good~a9cbe0ea.pl: Grupa wraca {dest_from} {nd_after} {goal_with}. {A} kładzie łup na stole i liczy go dwa razy.

exp_ret_good~73666a51.en: The quartermaster signs for {goal}: {A} and {B} came back from {dest} with more than anyone expected.
exp_ret_good~73666a51.pl: Kwatermistrz kwituje {goal_acc}: {A} i {B} wróci{AB?li|ły} {dest_from} z większym łupem, niż ktokolwiek się spodziewał.

exp_ret_good~63aa89fd.en: {A} and {B} come up the beach at dusk, bent under sacks of {goal}. The long house hums with it all evening.
exp_ret_good~63aa89fd.pl: {A} i {B} docierają o zmierzchu na plażę, zgięci pod workami {goal_gen}. Cały wieczór długi dom huczy od tej wieści.

exp_ret_good~51b34d7b.en: {A} grins the whole walk back from {dest}. {B} tells the story of getting the {goal} three times before supper.
exp_ret_good~51b34d7b.pl: {A} szczerzy zęby przez całą drogę {dest_from}. Historię zdobycia {goal_gen} {B} opowiada trzy razy przed kolacją.

exp_ret_good~d810c8be.en: {A} was right about {dest}: they came back with {goal}. {B} is already asking when they can go again.
exp_ret_good~d810c8be.pl: {A} miał{A?|a} rację co do {dest_gen}: wrócili {goal_with}. {B} już pyta, kiedy mogą iść znowu.

exp_ret_good~c60230c3.en: It was not much, but {A} and {B} came back from {dest} with {goal}, and tonight that counts.
exp_ret_good~c60230c3.pl: To niewiele, ale {A} i {B} wróci{AB?li|ły} {dest_from} {goal_with} i dziś to się liczy.

exp_ret_good~37aa044c.en: {A} drops a heavy bag by the door: {goal}, from {dest}. {B} follows with a second bag and a story about a dog that tracked them half the way.
exp_ret_good~37aa044c.pl: {A} rzuca przy drzwiach ciężką torbę {goal_with} {dest_from}. {B} wchodzi za {A?nim|nią} z drugą torbą i historią o psie, który szedł za nimi pół drogi.

exp_ret_good~de9da256.en: {A} comes through the gate with {goal} from {dest} and a look that says do not ask about the route.
exp_ret_good~de9da256.pl: {A} wchodzi przez bramę {goal_with} {dest_from} i miną, która mówi: nie pytajcie o trasę.

exp_ret_good~fef0f002.en: The weavers clear a place on the long table for {goal} from {dest}; {A} and {B} are given the first bowls of broth.
exp_ret_good~fef0f002.pl: Tkacze robią miejsce na długim stole na {goal_acc} {dest_from}; {A} i {B} dostają pierwsze miski zupy.

exp_ret_good~585c4eb2.en: {A} and {B} come back from {dest} {nd_after} with {goal}, and with the smell of somewhere else on their coats.
exp_ret_good~585c4eb2.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {dest_from} {nd_after} {goal_with}, a ich płaszcze pachną czymś innym.

exp_ret_good~d1f1694f.en: The bags are heavier than they look. {A} and {B} are back from {dest} {nd_after}, and pour {goal} out onto the table.
exp_ret_good~d1f1694f.pl: Torby są cięższe, niż wyglądają. {A} i {B} wracają {dest_from} {nd_after} i wysypują na stół {goal_acc}.

exp_ret_good~bc383a29.en: Somebody has been waiting at the gate since noon. {A} and {B} come in from {dest} {nd_after}, with {goal}, and are hugged by more people than they have ever met.
exp_ret_good~bc383a29.pl: Ktoś czeka przy bramie od południa. {A} i {B} wchodzą {dest_from} {nd_after} {goal_with} i są ściskan{AB?i|e} przez więcej osób, niż kiedykolwiek pozna{AB?li|ły}.

exp_ret_good~cc2b286f.en: Not a bad haul: {goal}, from {dest}. {A} wants a medal for it, and {B} wants it divided before anyone gets sentimental.
exp_ret_good~cc2b286f.pl: Niezły łup: {goal_nom}, {dest_from}. {A} chce za to medal, a {B} chce, żeby to podzielić, zanim ktoś się rozczuli.

exp_ret_good~1ad06090.en: {A} and {B} come back from {dest} {nd_after} with {goal} and a tin of peaches nobody can explain. The peaches go to the sick first.
exp_ret_good~1ad06090.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {dest_from} {nd_after} {goal_with} i z puszką brzoskwiń, której nikt nie umie wytłumaczyć. Brzoskwinie idą najpierw do chorych.

exp_ret_good~bda84607.en: {A} empties {A_his} pack onto the table piece by piece, {goal} from {dest}, and saves the best find for last: a pair of dry socks.
exp_ret_good~bda84607.pl: {A} wykłada na stół zawartość plecaka kawałek po kawałku, {goal} {dest_from}, a najlepsze zostawia na koniec: parę suchych skarpet.

exp_ret_good~34992134.en: {B} has a new limp and {A} has a new story, and between them they have {goal} from {dest}. The limp is from laughing, {B} claims.
exp_ret_good~34992134.pl: {B} od niedawna utyka, {A} ma nową historię, a razem mają {goal_acc} {dest_from}. To utykanie ze śmiechu, twierdzi {B}.

exp_ret_good~19c65f6d.en: The party is back from {dest} {nd_after}. {A} hands over {goal} and keeps one thing back: a child's drawing found on a fridge, folded small.
exp_ret_good~19c65f6d.pl: Grupa wraca {dest_from} {nd_after}. {A} oddaje {goal_acc}, a jedną rzecz zatrzymuje: dziecięcy rysunek z lodówki, złożony na małą kostkę.

exp_ret_good~b6ba0b83.en: {A} and {B} found {goal} at {dest} behind a false wall somebody built in the first year and never came back to. They leave a thank-you note.
exp_ret_good~b6ba0b83.pl: {A} i {B} znaleźli {dest_at} {goal_acc} za fałszywą ścianą, którą ktoś postawił w pierwszym roku i nigdy po to nie wrócił. Zostawiają kartkę z podziękowaniem.

exp_ret_good~444ab632.en: {A} comes through the gate whistling, with {goal} from {dest}. {B} walks in behind {A_him} with a face that says the whistling started miles ago.
exp_ret_good~444ab632.pl: {A} wchodzi przez bramę, gwiżdżąc, {goal_with} {dest_from}. {B} idzie za {A?nim|nią} z miną, która mówi, że gwizdanie zaczęło się wiele kilometrów temu.

exp_ret_good~26254781.en: {A} and {B} are back {nd_after} with {goal}. They had to leave half of it at {dest}; {A} has already drawn where it is hidden.
exp_ret_good~26254781.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {nd_after} {goal_with}. Połowę trzeba było zostawić {dest_at}; {A} już narysował{A?|a}, gdzie jest schowana.

exp_ret_good~82484f03.en: {goal}, from {dest}: less than hoped, more than nothing. {A} sets it down very carefully, as if it could still be dropped and lost.
exp_ret_good~82484f03.pl: {goal}, {dest_from}: mniej, niż liczono, więcej niż nic. {A} odkłada to bardzo ostrożnie, jakby wciąż mogło upaść i przepaść.

exp_ret_good~d2a857d6.en: {A} and {B} come home {nd_after} smelling of mildew and smoke, with {goal} from {dest}. Their clothes are boiled before they are allowed to sit.
exp_ret_good~d2a857d6.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {nd_after}, cuchnąc pleśnią i dymem, {goal_with} {dest_from}. Zanim pozwolą im usiąść, ich ubrania lądują w kotle.

exp_ret_good~576f6bde.en: {B} carried {goal} back from {dest} wrapped in a shower curtain with ducks on it. The shower curtain is now the clan's flag, unofficially.
exp_ret_good~576f6bde.pl: {B} {B?przyniósł|przyniosła} {goal_acc} {dest_from} w zasłonie prysznicowej w kaczki. Zasłona jest teraz nieoficjalną flagą klanu.

exp_ret_good~56eb73d4.en: {A} and {B} bring {goal} back from {dest} on a shopping cart with one wheel that screams. The whole FOB hears them coming from the street.
exp_ret_good~56eb73d4.pl: {A} i {B} przywożą {goal_acc} {dest_from} na wózku sklepowym z jednym wyjącym kołem. Cała baza słyszy ich już z ulicy.

exp_ret_good~0c6591f3.en: {A} reports to the quartermaster: {dest}, {goal}, no contact, all present. The quartermaster writes it down and, for once, says 'good'.
exp_ret_good~0c6591f3.pl: {A} melduje kwatermistrzowi: {dest}, {goal}, bez kontaktu, wszyscy obecni. Kwatermistrz zapisuje to i raz w życiu mówi 'dobrze'.

exp_ret_good~61728a6f.en: {A} and {B} pull the boat up the shingle with {goal} from {dest} under an oilcloth. The children run down to help and mostly get wet.
exp_ret_good~61728a6f.pl: {A} i {B} wyciągają łódź na kamienistą plażę, {goal} {dest_from} pod ceratą. Dzieci zbiegają pomóc i głównie mokną.

exp_ret_good~d78c790d.en: {A} lays {goal} from {dest} at the foot of the Prophet's picture before anyone may touch it. {B} waits, hungry, with folded hands.
exp_ret_good~d78c790d.pl: {A} składa {goal_acc} {dest_from} u stóp wizerunku Proroka, zanim ktokolwiek może tego dotknąć. {B} czeka, głodn{B?y|a}, ze złożonymi rękami.

exp_ret_empty~dbd83ec6.en: {A} and {B} are back from {dest} {nd_after} with nothing. The shelves were bare, and somebody had been there first.
exp_ret_empty~dbd83ec6.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {dest_from} {nd_after} z pustymi rękami. Półki były gołe, ktoś ich uprzedził.

exp_ret_empty~e7ea9fb0.en: Nothing at {dest}. {A} says it twice, as if the second time might change it, and goes to wash.
exp_ret_empty~e7ea9fb0.pl: Nic {dest_at}. {A} powtarza to dwa razy, jakby za drugim razem mogło się zmienić, i idzie się umyć.

exp_ret_empty~666a0af1.en: {A} and {B} found no {goal}. They found an empty can and one more reason to be tired.
exp_ret_empty~666a0af1.pl: {A} i {B} nie znaleźli {goal_gen}. Znaleźli pustą puszkę i jeszcze jeden powód do zmęczenia.

exp_ret_empty~e660d1b0.en: The trip to {dest} for {goal} came to nothing. {B} swears the place was picked clean a week ago.
exp_ret_empty~e660d1b0.pl: Wyprawa {dest_to} po {goal_acc} spełzła na niczym. {B} przysięga, że miejsce ogołocono tydzień temu.

exp_ret_empty~d86514c1.en: The map comes back from {dest} with one more crossing-out. {A} and {B} are home {nd_after}, without {goal}.
exp_ret_empty~d86514c1.pl: Mapa wraca z jednym skreśleniem więcej: {dest}. {A} i {B} są w domu {nd_after}, bez {goal_gen}.

exp_ret_empty~b8f6892b.en: The tide took the path to {dest}. {A} and {B} turn back with wet boots and no {goal}.
exp_ret_empty~b8f6892b.pl: Przypływ zabrał drogę {dest_to}. {A} i {B} zawracają z mokrymi butami i bez {goal_gen}.

exp_ret_empty~7bfd6dca.en: Scrappers had been through {dest} before them. {A} and {B} come back with a bent spoon and bad words.
exp_ret_empty~7bfd6dca.pl: Szabrownicy byli {dest_at} przed nimi. {A} i {B} wracają z wygiętą łyżką i brzydkimi słowami.

exp_ret_empty~634a9172.en: {A} and {B} come back from {dest} {nd_after} with a road atlas, a bag of marbles and no {goal}. The atlas is already out of date.
exp_ret_empty~634a9172.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {dest_from} {nd_after} z atlasem drogowym, woreczkiem kulek i bez {goal_gen}. Atlas jest już nieaktualny.

exp_ret_empty~7a18c3b0.en: Somebody had written GONE on the door at {dest}, and they were right. {A} and {B} are home {nd_after} without {goal}.
exp_ret_empty~7a18c3b0.pl: Ktoś napisał na drzwiach {dest_at} PUSTO i miał rację. {A} i {B} wracają {nd_after} bez {goal_gen}.

exp_ret_empty~eb915410.en: {A} walks straight past the table where the haul would go and lies down with {A_his} boots on. {dest} had no {goal}. {B} unlaces the boots.
exp_ret_empty~eb915410.pl: {A} przechodzi obok stołu, na którym miał leżeć łup, i kładzie się w butach. {dest_at} nie było {goal_gen}. {B} rozsznurowuje te buty.

exp_ret_empty~44e635ae.en: Nothing at {dest} but water damage and a dead radio. {B} brings the radio anyway, in case somebody here can wake it.
exp_ret_empty~44e635ae.pl: {dest}: nic, tylko zacieki i martwe radio. {B} i tak przynosi radio, na wypadek gdyby ktoś tu umiał je obudzić.

exp_ret_empty~ba59ef41.en: The shelves at {dest} were bare and there was a WLF tag on the wall, older than anyone at the FOB. {A} and {B} come home without {goal}.
exp_ret_empty~ba59ef41.pl: Półki {dest_at} były puste, a na ścianie widniał znak WLF z czasów, których nikt w bazie nie pamięta. {A} i {B} wracają bez {goal_gen}.

exp_ret_empty~0d12c709.en: {A} and {B} sit on the shore for an hour before they come up to the gate. {dest} gave them nothing, and they wanted to be ready to say so.
exp_ret_empty~0d12c709.pl: {A} i {B} siedzą godzinę na brzegu, zanim podejdą do bramy. {dest_at} nie znaleźli nic, a chcieli być gotowi, żeby to powiedzieć.

exp_ret_hurt~dfa7b43d.en: {B} helps {A} home from {dest}. {A_He} has {inj}, but the {goal} made it back.
exp_ret_hurt~dfa7b43d.pl: {B} pomaga {A?mu|jej} wrócić {dest_from}. {A} ma {inj_acc}, ale udało się przynieść {goal_acc}.

exp_ret_hurt~f7c678f4.en: Back from {dest} with {goal}, and with {inj} for {A}. Rest will fix it, everyone agrees, which is what people say when they do not know.
exp_ret_hurt~f7c678f4.pl: Wracają {dest_from} {goal_with}, a {A} ma {inj_acc}. Odpoczynek to naprawi, zgadzają się wszyscy, czyli tak, jak się mówi, kiedy się nie wie.

exp_ret_hurt~7acf382c.en: A bad fall at {dest}: {A} has {inj}. Still, {B} carries the {goal} home in {A}'s coat.
exp_ret_hurt~7acf382c.pl: Niefortunny upadek {dest_at}: {A} ma {inj_acc}. Mimo to {B} niesie {goal_acc} w {A?jego|jej} płaszczu.

exp_ret_hurt~4573f506.en: {A} has {inj} after a clicker got too close at {dest}. {B} still got the {goal} out.
exp_ret_hurt~4573f506.pl: {A} ma {inj_acc} po bliskim spotkaniu z klikaczem {dest_at}. {B} zdołał{B?|a} jednak wynieść {goal_acc}.

exp_ret_hurt~c88d3ddb.en: A slick rock at {dest} and a wet fall: {A} has {inj}. {B} carries the {goal} the rest of the way, saying nothing, which is its own kind of kindness.
exp_ret_hurt~c88d3ddb.pl: Śliski kamień {dest_at} i mokry upadek: {A} ma {inj_acc}. {B} niesie {goal_acc} do końca drogi, nic nie mówiąc, co też jest formą życzliwości.

exp_ret_hurt~8235ef87.en: {A} came back from {dest} with {goal} and {inj}, from a staircase that was there until {A} stood on it.
exp_ret_hurt~8235ef87.pl: {A} wróci{A?ł|ła} {dest_from} {goal_with} i {inj_with}, przez schody, które były, dopóki {A} na nich nie stan{A?ął|ęła}.

exp_ret_hurt~ab349422.en: {B} had to splint {A}'s {inj} with a ruler at {dest}. It held all the way home, and so did {goal}.
exp_ret_hurt~ab349422.pl: {dest_at} {B} musiał{B?|a} usztywnić linijką uraz, z którym wraca {A}: {inj_nom}. Linijka wytrzymała całą drogę do domu, tak samo jak {goal}.

exp_ret_hurt~081ec61e.en: {A} has {inj} and a long face, but {goal} is home from {dest}, and the long face is mostly about a lost hat.
exp_ret_hurt~081ec61e.pl: {A} ma {inj_acc} i długą minę, ale {goal} jest już w domu {dest_from}, a długa mina dotyczy głównie zgubionej czapki.

exp_ret_hurt~10966d8a.en: {A} took {inj} getting over a fence at {dest} with a dog behind {A_him}. The dog was not one of ours. {B} carried {goal}.
exp_ret_hurt~10966d8a.pl: {A} nabawi{A?ł|ła} się {inj_gen} na płocie {dest_at}, z psem na karku. To nie był nasz pies. {B} {B?niósł|niosła} {goal_acc}.

exp_ret_hurt~4c734505.en: The boat hit rocks off {dest} and {A} has {inj} for it. {B} bailed with a hat all the way back and saved {goal}.
exp_ret_hurt~4c734505.pl: Łódź uderzyła w skały {dest_at} i {A} ma przez to {inj_acc}. {B} całą drogę wybierał{B?|a} wodę czapką i ocalił{B?|a} {goal_acc}.

exp_ret_contact~ff0acb9d.en: {A} and {B} saw a {enemy} patrol at {dest} and lay still in the dark until it passed. The {goal} will have to wait.
exp_ret_contact~ff0acb9d.pl: {A} i {B} zobaczy{AB?li|ły} patrol {enemy_gen} {dest_at} i le{AB?żeli|żały} bez ruchu w ciemności, aż przeszedł. Po {goal_acc} pójdą innym razem.

exp_ret_contact~3c5837c1.en: Fresh boot prints around {dest}: the {enemies} are looking for the same thing. {A} and {B} come home early and say little about how close it was.
exp_ret_contact~3c5837c1.pl: Świeże ślady butów wokół {dest_gen}: {enemy} szukają tego samego. {A} i {B} wracają wcześniej i niewiele mówią o tym, jak blisko było.

exp_ret_contact~3f6eecdd.en: {A} traded a lighter for {goal} with a lone {enemy} scout at {dest}, who did not want the shooting either. Nobody says that out loud.
exp_ret_contact~3f6eecdd.pl: {A} wymienił{A?|a} zapalniczkę na {goal_acc} z samotnym zwiadowcą {enemy_gen} {dest_at}, który też nie chciał strzelaniny. Nikt nie mówi tego na głos.

exp_ret_contact~e7ca898a.en: Gunfire at {dest}. {A} and {B} get out through a drain and come back without the {goal}, shaking.
exp_ret_contact~e7ca898a.pl: Strzelanina {dest_at}. {A} i {B} uciekają kanałem i wracają bez {goal_gen}, dygocząc.

exp_ret_inf~17849e48.en: A {inf} was waiting in the dark at {dest}. {A} and {B} back out the way they came, quietly, and will try for {goal} somewhere else.
exp_ret_inf~17849e48.pl: {dest_at} w ciemności czekał {inf}. {A} i {B} wycofują się tą samą drogą, po cichu, i spróbują po {goal_acc} gdzie indziej.

exp_ret_inf~129c4e0e.en: {A} counts {infs} at {dest}: too many for two people. {B} wants to go in anyway. They do not, and nobody calls it cowardice.
exp_ret_inf~129c4e0e.pl: {A} nalicza {infs_gen} {dest_at}: za dużo jak na dwie osoby. {B} i tak chce wejść. Nie wchodzą i nikt nie nazywa tego tchórzostwem.

exp_ret_inf~ac51a4d9.en: {A} and {B} are back from {dest} with the {goal}, and with a story: a {inf}, a locked door, and a very short sprint.
exp_ret_inf~ac51a4d9.pl: {A} i {B} wracają {dest_from} {goal_with} i z historią: {inf}, zamknięte drzwi i bardzo krótki sprint.

exp_lost~19f221ee.en: {A} says the party lost {D} near {dest}. It was quick, {A_he} says, and says it again, as if saying it enough would make it true.
exp_lost~19f221ee.pl: {A} mówi, że w pobliżu {dest_gen} grupa straciła kogoś: {D}. Stało się to szybko, mówi {A}, i mówi to jeszcze raz, jakby wystarczająco częste powtarzanie miało uczynić to prawdą.

exp_lost~f5accbbf.en: The party came back from {dest} one short. The pack {D} carried sits by the door, and nobody touches it.
exp_lost~f5accbbf.pl: Grupa wróciła {dest_from} w mniejszym składzie. Plecak, który nosi{D?ł|ła} {D}, stoi przy drzwiach i nikt go nie rusza.

exp_lost~0d9773cf.en: {A} tries to explain what happened to {D} at {dest} and gives up halfway through the sentence.
exp_lost~0d9773cf.pl: {D}: {A} próbuje wyjaśnić, co stało się {dest_at}, i rezygnuje w połowie zdania.

exp_recall~dd15aea7.en: {A} cuts the trip to {dest} short: {B} is not fit to walk any farther, and {A} will not leave {B_him} behind.
exp_recall~dd15aea7.pl: {A} skraca wyprawę {dest_to}: {B} nie da rady iść dalej, a {A} nie zostawi {B?go|jej} samego.

exp_recall~e6e1d6c2.en: The party turns back from {dest} before it has found {goal}. {B} is struggling, and {A} makes the call.
exp_recall~e6e1d6c2.pl: Grupa zawraca {dest_from}, zanim znalazła {goal_acc}. {B} ledwo idzie, a decyzję podejmuje {A}.

inj_mid~7348ffd5.en: {A} is on light duty with {inj}: sorting jars, mending coats and offering opinions nobody asked for.
inj_mid~7348ffd5.pl: {A} ma lekką służbę z powodu {inj_gen}: sortuje słoiki, łata płaszcze i rozdaje opinie, o które nikt nie prosił.

inj_mid~be5f8ce1.en: {A} still has {inj}, better than yesterday. {A_He} will not admit it hurts.
inj_mid~be5f8ce1.pl: {A} wciąż ma {inj_acc}, ale lepiej niż wczoraj. {A?On|Ona} nie przyzna, że boli.

inj_mid~6fa69ba7.en: {A} sits by the fire with {inj} and a pile of work that can be done sitting down.
inj_mid~6fa69ba7.pl: {A} siedzi przy ogniu {inj_with} i stosem roboty, którą da się wykonać na siedząco.

inj_mid~97e0ed7c.en: {A} jokes about {inj} all through supper. {B} laughs, and then carries {A}'s bowl without being asked.
inj_mid~97e0ed7c.pl: {A} żartuje na temat {inj_gen} przez całą kolację. {B} się śmieje, a potem bez proszenia niesie {A?jego|jej} miskę.

inj_mid~71bf5895.en: {A} says it is nothing. {A_He} has now said so four times today, and nobody believes it.
inj_mid~71bf5895.pl: {A} mówi, że to nic. Powtórzył{A?|a} to dziś już cztery razy i nikt w to nie wierzy.

inj_mid~259be0a0.en: {A} peels potatoes one-handed because of {inj}, and is somehow faster than anyone with two.
inj_mid~259be0a0.pl: {A} obiera ziemniaki jedną ręką przez {inj_acc} i jakimś cudem robi to szybciej niż ktokolwiek dwiema.

inj_mid~3476b745.en: {A} has been put on the mending pile with {inj}. Three coats, a tarp and {B}'s trousers, which {B} did not know were torn.
inj_mid~3476b745.pl: {A} {inj_with} trafi{A?ł|ła} do sterty cerowania. Trzy kurtki, plandeka i spodnie, o których dziurze {B} nie miał{B?|a} pojęcia.

inj_mid~957e058b.en: {A} keeps forgetting {inj} until {A_he} tries to lift something. Then the whole yard hears that {A_he} remembered.
inj_mid~957e058b.pl: {A} ciągle zapomina, że ma {inj_acc}, dopóki nie spróbuje czegoś podnieść. Wtedy całe podwórze słyszy, że sobie przypomniał{A?|a}.

inj_heal~54916e2c.en: {A} no longer has {inj} and goes back on the rota. The others pretend they never doubted it.
inj_heal~54916e2c.pl: {A} nie ma już {inj_gen} i wraca do grafiku. Reszta udaje, że nigdy nie wątpiła.

inj_heal~35011475.en: {A} is back to full work today. {B} makes a show of handing over the heavy end of the load.
inj_heal~35011475.pl: {A} wraca dziś do pełnej pracy. {B} demonstracyjnie oddaje {A?mu|jej} cięższy koniec ciężaru.

inj_heal~9ab5a76f.en: {A} carries a full bucket across the yard to prove that {inj} is gone, and spills none of it out of pride.
inj_heal~9ab5a76f.pl: {A} przenosi przez podwórze pełne wiadro, żeby udowodnić, że {inj_nom} to przeszłość, i z dumy nie rozlewa ani kropli.

inj_heal~e015825b.en: {A} hands back the walking stick, washed. {B} hangs it by the door for the next one.
inj_heal~e015825b.pl: {A} oddaje laskę, umytą. {B} wiesza ją przy drzwiach dla następnej osoby.

proj_start~e5bdf9fb.en: {A} stakes out the ground for {proj}. {B} gets the shovel and a doubtful look.
proj_start~e5bdf9fb.pl: {A} wyznacza miejsce pod {proj_acc}. {B} dostaje łopatę i niepewną minę.

proj_start~8f9d1d4a.en: The plans for {proj} come out of a drawer, stained and folded in eight. {A} reads them aloud; {B} nods as if they made sense.
proj_start~8f9d1d4a.pl: Plany {proj_gen} wychodzą z szuflady, poplamione i złożone w ósemkę. {A} czyta je na głos, a {B} kiwa głową, jakby miały sens.

proj_start~06228618.en: After the evening reading, {A} stands and announces work on {proj}. The whole long house hears it; {B} is the first to offer {B_his} hands.
proj_start~06228618.pl: Po wieczornym czytaniu {A} wstaje i zapowiada prace nad {proj_ins}. Cały długi dom to słyszy; {B} pierwsz{B?y|a} ofiarowuje swoje ręce.

proj_start~4a1e7539.en: Isaac signs off on {proj}. {A} gets the job and {B} gets whatever is left of the manpower and the sleep.
proj_start~4a1e7539.pl: Isaac zatwierdza prace nad {proj_ins}. {A} dostaje to zadanie, a {B} to, co zostanie z ludzi i ze snu.

proj_start~aa808843.en: Work on {proj} starts today. {A} and {B} argue about the first nail for a good ten minutes, which everybody agrees is a good sign.
proj_start~aa808843.pl: Dziś ruszają prace nad {proj_ins}. {A} i {B} kłócą się o pierwszy gwóźdź dobre dziesięć minut, co wszyscy uznają za dobry znak.

proj_start~80c03e9e.en: Nobody has the strength, but {proj} cannot wait. {A} starts alone; after an hour {B} comes out and picks up the other end.
proj_start~80c03e9e.pl: Nikt nie ma siły, ale prace nad {proj_ins} nie mogą czekać. {A} zaczyna sam{A?|a}; po godzinie wychodzi {B} i chwyta drugi koniec.

proj_start~7050d23a.en: Spirits are up, so {A} picks the day to begin {proj}. {B} brings tea for the diggers before they have dug anything.
proj_start~7050d23a.pl: Nastroje są dobre, więc {A} wybiera ten dzień na początek prac nad {proj_ins}. {B} przynosi herbatę dla kopaczy, zanim cokolwiek wykopią.

proj_start~ac08024d.en: {A} paces out {proj} with a length of rope knotted every yard. {B} follows with a bag of tent pegs and a doubtful silence.
proj_start~ac08024d.pl: {A} odmierza {proj_acc} kawałkiem liny z węzłem co metr. {B} idzie za {A?nim|nią} z workiem śledzi i powątpiewającym milczeniem.

proj_start~6b71be29.en: Work on {proj} starts with taking something else apart: {A} and {B} strip the old shed for its nails.
proj_start~6b71be29.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} zaczynają się od rozbierania czegoś innego: {A} i {B} rozbierają starą szopę na gwoździe.

proj_start~5f9362ff.en: {A} has drawn {proj} on the back of a calendar from 2013. {B} studies the drawing and then the month it is drawn over.
proj_start~5f9362ff.pl: {A} narysował{A?|a} {proj_acc} na odwrocie kalendarza z 2013 roku. {B} ogląda rysunek, a potem miesiąc, na którym powstał.

proj_start~5ca3b403.en: {A} breaks ground for {proj} and finds a buried toy car in the first shovel. {B} declares it the clan's foundation stone.
proj_start~5ca3b403.pl: {A} wbija pierwszą łopatę pod {proj_acc} i wykopuje zakopany samochodzik. {B} ogłasza go kamieniem węgielnym klanu.

proj_start~b104a6c3.en: {proj} is started on an empty stomach, which {A} says is the only way anything gets started here. {B} carries the first load.
proj_start~b104a6c3.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} zaczynają się na pusty żołądek, a {A} twierdzi, że tylko tak da się tu cokolwiek zacząć. {B} niesie pierwszy ładunek.

proj_start~1d9dbf28.en: {A} gets written permission for {proj} on a WLF requisition form, in triplicate. {B} gets a hammer.
proj_start~1d9dbf28.pl: {A} dostaje pisemną zgodę na {proj_acc} na formularzu zapotrzebowania WLF, w trzech egzemplarzach. {B} dostaje młotek.

proj_start~f163c09a.en: The elders mark the ground for {proj} with white stones and a hymn. {A} and {B} begin digging when the last verse ends.
proj_start~f163c09a.pl: Starsi znaczą teren pod {proj_acc} białymi kamieniami i hymnem. {A} i {B} zaczynają kopać, gdy kończy się ostatnia zwrotka.

proj_prog~86fd4de3.en: {B} measures twice and tells {A} the whole thing is crooked. {A} measures once and says it is not. The work is {prog}.
proj_prog~86fd4de3.pl: {B} mierzy dwa razy i mówi {A?mu|jej}, że to krzywe. {A} mierzy raz i mówi, że nie. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~064bc657.en: The work on {proj} goes on between prayers and meals. {A} and {B} take the day shift; the work is {prog}.
proj_prog~064bc657.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} toczą się między modlitwą a posiłkami. {A} i {B} mają zmianę dzienną; prace {prog}.

proj_prog~a9bc815a.en: {A} and {B} scrounge nails from the old fence for {proj}. The work is {prog}, and the fence is not looking good.
proj_prog~a9bc815a.pl: {A} i {B} wyciągają gwoździe ze starego ogrodzenia na potrzeby prac nad {proj_ins}. Prace {prog}, a ogrodzenie nie wygląda dobrze.

proj_prog~f7468fe4.en: {A} brings a measuring string from somewhere, and for two days nobody builds anything without checking it. The work on {proj} is {prog}.
proj_prog~f7468fe4.pl: {A} przynosi skądś miarkę ze sznurka i przez dwa dni nikt nie buduje niczego bez sprawdzenia. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~9951674f.en: {A} hangs a bucket of nails from {A_his} belt and does not come down off {proj} until dark. By then it is {prog}.
proj_prog~9951674f.pl: {A} przywiesza sobie do pasa wiadro gwoździ i nie schodzi z budowy aż do zmroku. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~a903fe11.en: {B} saws, {A} holds, and they switch whenever one of them swears. {proj}: {prog}.
proj_prog~a903fe11.pl: {B} piłuje, {A} trzyma, a zamieniają się, gdy któreś zaklnie. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~46dac36c.en: Somebody's old door becomes part of {proj} today, knob and all. {A} says the knob stays. {proj} is {prog}.
proj_prog~46dac36c.pl: Czyjeś stare drzwi stają się dziś częścią budowy, razem z klamką. {A} upiera się, że klamka zostaje. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~6eb0f058.en: {A} pulls out yesterday's work on {proj} and does it again, properly, while {B} watches with folded arms. It is still {prog}.
proj_prog~6eb0f058.pl: {A} rozbiera wczorajszą robotę i robi ją jeszcze raz, porządnie, a {B} patrzy z założonymi rękami. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~b6862343.en: The children have been set to straightening bent nails for {proj}. {A} pays them one raisin per ten nails. {proj} is {prog}.
proj_prog~b6862343.pl: Dzieci prostują krzywe gwoździe na budowę. {A} płaci im jedną rodzynkę za dziesięć gwoździ. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~d3f482a4.en: {A} and {B} work on {proj} trading verses of a song, the words made up as they go. It is {prog}.
proj_prog~d3f482a4.pl: {A} i {B} pracują przy budowie, śpiewając na zmianę po zwrotce, ze słowami wymyślanymi na bieżąco. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~c26f5f06.en: {A} works slowly on {proj}, resting between every board, and nobody tells {A_him} to hurry. {proj} is {prog}.
proj_prog~c26f5f06.pl: {A} pracuje powoli, odpoczywając po każdej desce, i nikt {A?go|jej} nie pogania. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~a41774ee.en: A board for {proj} turns out to be a road sign, face down. {A} turns it up: EXIT 165. It goes in anyway, sign side in. {proj}: {prog}.
proj_prog~a41774ee.pl: Deska na budowę okazuje się znakiem drogowym, leżącym napisem w dół. {A} odwraca go: ZJAZD 165. I tak idzie do roboty, napisem do środka. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~aafa4006.en: {B} drops the level off {proj} and it is the only level. {A} finds the bubble still whole after an hour on {A_his} knees. {proj} is {prog}.
proj_prog~aafa4006.pl: {B} upuszcza poziomicę z rusztowania, a to jedyna poziomica. {A} po godzinie na kolanach stwierdza, że pęcherzyk jest cały. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~8e257335.en: Rain stops work on {proj} at noon. {A} and {B} stand under it, the part that is already roofed, and call that progress. It is {prog}.
proj_prog~8e257335.pl: Deszcz przerywa prace w południe. {A} i {B} stoją pod tą częścią, która ma już dach, i nazywają to postępem. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~0f65e3f4.en: {A} borrows a ladder from the motor pool for {proj} and does not mention that it is being borrowed. {proj} is {prog}.
proj_prog~0f65e3f4.pl: {A} pożycza drabinę z warsztatu na budowę i nie wspomina, że to pożyczka. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~a62e6028.en: Off-shift soldiers wander over to watch the work on {proj} and stay to argue about it. {A} hands each one a plank. It is {prog}.
proj_prog~a62e6028.pl: Żołnierze po służbie przychodzą popatrzeć na budowę i zostają się pokłócić. {A} wręcza każdemu deskę. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~8d1ac18b.en: {A} sings the building hymn while {B} lashes the poles of {proj} with wet rope that tightens as it dries. It is {prog}.
proj_prog~8d1ac18b.pl: {A} śpiewa hymn budowniczych, a {B} wiąże tyczki mokrą liną, która zaciska się, gdy schnie. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_prog~589c407d.en: Driftwood for {proj} has been drying in the long house for a week, and everyone has tripped over it at least once. {proj}: {prog}.
proj_prog~589c407d.pl: Drewno z plaży na budowę suszy się w długim domu od tygodnia i każdy zdążył się o nie potknąć. Prace nad {proj_ins} {prog}.

proj_stall~11c5afed.en: Work on {proj} stops: {A} and {B} are out looking for food instead.
proj_stall~11c5afed.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} stanęły: {A} i {B} zamiast tego szukają jedzenia.

proj_stall~e4dda61a.en: The tools for {proj} lie where they were dropped. {A} says they will pick them up tomorrow, when there is something in their stomachs.
proj_stall~e4dda61a.pl: Narzędzia do prac nad {proj_ins} leżą tam, gdzie je rzucono. {A} mówi, że podniosą je jutro, kiedy coś będą mieli w brzuchach.

proj_stall~9f6b228f.en: {B} covers {proj} with a tarp and sets a stone on every corner. It will keep until there is something to eat.
proj_stall~9f6b228f.pl: {B} przykrywa {proj_acc} plandeką i kładzie kamień na każdym rogu. Poczeka, aż będzie co jeść.

proj_stall~283c1262.en: Nobody has touched {proj} in days. {A} walks past it on the way to the latrine and looks the other way.
proj_stall~283c1262.pl: Nikt od dni nie dotknął budowy. {A} przechodzi obok w drodze do latryny i patrzy w drugą stronę.

proj_stall~bc0eeaa4.en: The saw for {proj} has gone missing, and the work with it. {B} suspects the cooks.
proj_stall~bc0eeaa4.pl: Zginęła piła do budowy, a razem z nią robota. {B} podejrzewa kucharzy.

proj_done~2f4a8ead.en: The work on {proj} is finished. {A} steps back, wipes {A_his} hands and says nothing, which is the highest praise {A_he} knows.
proj_done~2f4a8ead.pl: Koniec prac nad {proj_ins}. {A} odsuwa się o krok, ociera dłonie i nic nie mówi, a to najwyższa pochwała, jaką zna.

proj_done~4d06cc6f.en: The work on {proj} is done, and {B} insists on a toast with the last of the tea. {A} accepts, modestly, twice.
proj_done~4d06cc6f.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} skończone; {B} nalega na toast resztką herbaty. {A} przyjmuje go skromnie, dwa razy.

proj_done~66c0e1f8.en: {A} nails the last board in the work on {proj}. The first thing anyone does with it is lean on it, to be sure.
proj_done~66c0e1f8.pl: {A} przybija ostatnią deskę w ramach prac nad {proj_ins}. Pierwsze, co robi każdy, to oprzeć się o nią, żeby się upewnić.

proj_done~08378643.en: Against all odds, the work on {proj} is finished. Nobody cheers; people just stand and look at it for a while.
proj_done~08378643.pl: Wbrew wszelkim szansom prace nad {proj_ins} są skończone. Nikt nie wiwatuje; ludzie po prostu stoją i patrzą na to przez chwilę.

proj_done~61e603e6.en: {A} and {B} finish the work on {proj} and stand looking at it as if it might say something.
proj_done~61e603e6.pl: {A} i {B} kończą prace nad {proj_ins} i stoją, patrząc na to, jakby miało coś powiedzieć.

proj_done~d6a699a6.en: The work on {proj} is done, and the whole camp comes to look. {A} is embarrassed; {B} is proud enough for both.
proj_done~d6a699a6.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} skończone i cały obóz przychodzi popatrzeć. {A} jest zawstydzon{A?y|a}, a {B} dumn{B?y|a} za oboje.

proj_done~9e163166.en: The work on {proj} is done. {A} checks it twice, {B} once, and they agree that it will hold.
proj_done~9e163166.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} skończone. {A} sprawdza je dwa razy, {B} raz i uzgadniają, że wytrzyma.

proj_done~dd12affa.en: {proj} is finished. {A} carves the date into it and, after some thought, {B}'s initials too, because {B} did the boring parts.
proj_done~dd12affa.pl: Prace nad {proj_ins} skończone. {A} wycina w drewnie datę, a po namyśle także inicjały: {B} robił{B?|a} nudne kawałki.

proj_done~b67f0eeb.en: The last nail goes into {proj} at dusk. {A} hammers it in very slowly, so that everyone has time to come and watch.
proj_done~b67f0eeb.pl: Ostatni gwóźdź wchodzi w {proj_acc} o zmierzchu. {A} wbija go bardzo powoli, żeby każdy zdążył przyjść i popatrzeć.
